history-friendship.title: Friends who stay near
history-friendship.caption: A friend gently brushes an older woman’s hair as they talk. The Lord reminded Joseph that his friends still stood by him; ordinary acts of care can give that friendship a present-day expression.
history-friendship.period: Contemporary home setting, no exact date
history-friendship.basis: D&C121 from Joseph Smith’s1839 confinement assures friendship and teaches gentle influence. New anonymous modern hair-care scene is an application, not Joseph’s recorded history.
history-friendship.unknown: No real people, illness, dependency, family relation or historical occurrence asserted.
history-friendship.unique: Prison visit rejected because existing collection-art-review-4 includes that action. Bedside, phonecall, modern scripture reading and garden work excluded. Specific hair brushing between adult friends is distinct in searched filename/review/HTML inventory.
characters: Older adult with natural silver hair and lined face

pioneers-traveler.title: Make room in the journey
pioneers-traveler.caption: Before leaving, a traveler and her companion make sure her bag and walker will be ready for the journey. The preparations in Doctrine and Covenants136 ask us to notice whose needs might otherwise be overlooked.
pioneers-traveler.period: Contemporary residential departure, no exact date
pioneers-traveler.basis: January14,1847 Winter Quarters revelation instructs preparations for travelers and those remaining, including poor, widows, fatherless and army families. Contemporary departure is an application, not exact reenactment.
pioneers-traveler.unknown: No real person, medical condition or specific trip asserted. Older traveler participates and directs her preferences.
pioneers-traveler.unique: Distinct from existing roadside phone assistance, umbrella kindness, walker waiting behind branch clearing and nineteenth-century journey scenes; specific action is preparing her bag/walker before departure.
characters: Older adult alert and participating, silver hair

temple-tribute.title: The Son and the temple tribute
temple-tribute.caption: In Capernaum, Jesus speaks with Peter about the temple tribute and sends him to the sea with a hook. The account invites us to consider who Jesus is as the Son, even as He provides for the payment.
temple-tribute.period: Early first century AD, mortal ministry in Capernaum
temple-tribute.basis: Matthew17:24-27 identifies Capernaum and instruction in house, children being free, then hook/fish/payment. Cross-reference Exodus30:13 identifies tribute background. Depict instruction before fishing, not Christ at shore or modern ordinances.
temple-tribute.unknown: Exact date, Peter birth/age, room details, garment colors and line preparation staging not stated. No precise chronology or ancient authenticated likeness claim.
temple-tribute.unique: Existing tribute-coin is Matthew22 Caesar question, not Matthew17 temple tribute. New indoor seated two-person preparation differs from standing courtyard John6 and public temple John7. Existing Temple scenes all preserved.
characters: Adult mortal ministry, approximately early thirties
Adult; exact age unknown; approved rear-profile continuity only

handcart-supplies.title: Help begins with willing hands
handcart-supplies.caption: Volunteers gather quilts, flour and clothing for the relief wagons. The first rescuers leave Salt Lake City on October7,1856, carrying help toward people still far out on the trail.
handcart-supplies.basis: Official article documents call October5, first departure two days later, warm clear local weather, donated quilts/flour/clothing and volunteer participation. Collective scene not exact documented individuals or exchange.
handcart-supplies.unknown: Specific volunteers, exact yard/wagon and every garment/hand action are interpretations. No named leader or precise birthdate asserted.
handcart-supplies.unique: Inspected actual Eleazer coin-counting donation and history practical-care sewing; new outdoor wagon-loading action differs. No duplicate blizzard rescue, river crossing or handcart hauling.
